1426.8: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Saloks, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). You have not sung the praises of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), (and) you have made your life worthless. Says Nanak, worship the Lord, O mind, as the fish (loves) the water. ॥1॥
1426.9: Why are you absorbed in the pleasures of the senses? Not for an instant do you turn away (from them). Says Nanak, worship the Lord, O mind, (and) the noose of Jam (the messenger of Death) does not fall (on you). ॥2॥
1426.10: Youth has gone by just like this (in vain), and old age has conquered the body. Says Nanak, worship the Lord, O mind; your span of life is slipping away. ॥3॥
1426.11: You have grown old, yet you do not see (that) death has arrived. Says Nanak, O crazed man, why do you not worship God? ॥4॥
1426.12: Wealth, wife and all your property: do not take them as your own. None of these is (your) companion; O Nanak, know this to be true. ॥5॥
1426.13: The Lord is the saviour of the fallen, the dispeller of fear, the Master of the masterless. Says Nanak, he is to be known as one who dwells with you always. ॥6॥
1426.14: The One who gave you body and wealth: with him you formed no love. Says Nanak, O crazed man, why do you waver now, helpless? ॥7॥
1426.15: The One who has given body, wealth, property, comforts and fine dwellings — says Nanak, listen, O mind: why do you not remember him, Ram? ॥8॥
1426.16: Ram is the giver of all comforts; there is no other. Says Nanak, listen, O mind: remembering him, the highest state is reached. ॥9॥
1427.1: The One by remembering whom the highest state is reached: worship him, my friend. Says Nanak, listen, O mind: your span of life grows shorter every day. ॥10॥
1427.2: (God) has fashioned the body of the five elements; know this, O clever and wise one. O Nanak, be sure of it: it will merge back into that from which it sprang. ॥11॥
The five elements: earth, water, fire, air and ether.
1427.3: The Lord dwells in every heart; the Sants have proclaimed it aloud. Says Nanak, worship him, O mind, (and) you will cross over the world-ocean. ॥12॥
1427.4: One whom neither pleasure nor pain touches, nor greed, attachment and pride — says Nanak, listen, O mind: he is the very image of God. ॥13॥
1427.5: One for whom there is neither praise nor slander, to whom gold and iron are alike — says Nanak, listen, O mind: know him to be liberated. ॥14॥
1427.6: One who knows neither joy nor grief, to whom foe and friend are alike — says Nanak, listen, O mind: know him to be liberated. ॥15॥
1427.7: One who puts fear into no one, and yields to no other's fear — says Nanak, listen, O mind: call him wise. ॥16॥
1427.8: One who has given up all of Maya's poison and taken on the garb of detachment — says Nanak, listen, O mind: (good) fortune is written on that man's forehead. ॥17॥
1427.9: One who has given up Maya and possessiveness, and has become detached from all — says Nanak, listen, O mind: in his heart God dwells. ॥18॥
1427.10: The mortal who has given up Haumai (ego), recognising Ram, the Creator — says Nanak, that man is liberated; O mind, take this as true. ॥19॥
1427.11: In Kalyug the Lord's Name destroys fear and takes away evil-mindedness. O Nanak, whoever dwells on (it) night and day, his works bear fruit. ॥20॥
1427.12: With the tongue, repeat the praises of Gobind; with the ears, hear the Lord's Name. Says Nanak, listen, O mind: (then) you will not fall into the abode of Jam. ॥21॥
1427.13: The mortal who gives up possessiveness, greed, attachment and pride — says Nanak, he himself crosses over and saves others too. ॥22॥
1427.14: As a dream is, and a show, so know the world to be. O Nanak, apart from God, nothing in all this is true. ॥23॥
1427.15: For Maya's sake the mortal ever wavers, night and day. O Nanak, among millions there is barely one with Narayan in his mind. ॥24॥
1427.16: As a bubble ever rises from the water and bursts, so is the world's creation made; says Nanak, listen, my friend. ॥25॥
1427.17: Blinded by the intoxication of Maya, the mortal is mindful of nothing. Says Nanak, without the Lord's worship, the noose of Jam falls upon him. ॥26॥
1427.18: If one longs for peace, let him take the refuge of Ram for ever. Says Nanak, listen, O mind: the human body is hard to obtain. ॥27॥
1427.19: Foolish, ignorant people run about after Maya. Says Nanak, without the Lord's worship, (their) life passes in vain. ॥28॥
1427.20: The mortal who worships (God) night and day: know him to be the form of Ram. Between the Lord's servant and the Lord there is no difference; O Nanak, take this as true. ॥29॥
1428.1: (One whose) mind stays caught in Maya, (who) has forgotten the Name of Gobind — says Nanak, without the Lord's worship, of what use is (his) life? ॥30॥
1428.2: Blinded by the intoxication of Maya, the mortal is not mindful of Ram. Says Nanak, without the Lord's worship, the noose of Jam falls upon him. ॥31॥
1428.3: In good times many become companions; in sorrow no one stands by. Says Nanak, worship the Lord, O mind; at the end (he alone) is (your) help. ॥32॥
1428.4: You have wandered birth after birth, yet the fear of Jam has not been erased. Says Nanak, worship the Lord, O mind, (and) you will find a dwelling free of fear. ॥33॥
1428.5: I have made many efforts, yet the pride of the mind is not erased. Nanak is caught in evil-mindedness; O God, save (me). ॥34॥
1428.6: Childhood, youth, and then old age: know them as the three stages (of life). Says Nanak, without the Lord's worship, take them all as wasted. ॥35॥
1428.7: What you had to do, you did not do; you fell into the snare of greed. O Nanak, the time has slipped away; why do you weep now, blind one? ॥36॥
1428.8: The mind is steeped in Maya and does not come out (of it), my friend, O Nanak, as a figure painted (on a wall) does not leave the wall. ॥37॥
1428.9: Man wants one thing, but it turns out quite another. He kept scheming to deceive; O Nanak, (meanwhile Death's) noose fell around (his) neck. ॥38॥
1428.10: Many efforts (man) has made for comfort, none for sorrow; says Nanak, listen, O mind: what pleases the Lord, that alone comes to pass. ॥39॥
1428.11: The world goes about as a beggar; Ram is the giver to all. Says Nanak, remember him, O mind, (and your) tasks will be fulfilled. ॥40॥
1428.12: Why does (one) take pride in what is false? Know the world to be like a dream. Nothing in all this is yours; Nanak has said this plainly. ॥41॥
1428.13: (Man) takes pride in the body, (which) is gone in a moment, my friend. O Nanak, the mortal who has uttered the Lord's praise has won the world. ॥42॥
1428.14: One in whose heart is the remembrance of Ram: know that man to be liberated. Between that man and the Lord there is no difference; O Nanak, take this as true. ॥43॥
1428.15: The mortal in whose mind there is no devotion to the one God — O Nanak, take his body to be like that of a swine or a dog. ॥44॥
1428.16: As a dog never at any time forsakes its master's house, O Nanak, so worship the Lord, with one mind and one heart. ॥45॥
1428.17: (One who) bathes at tiraths, keeps fasts and gives in charity, and holds pride in his mind — O Nanak, (these deeds) of his go for nothing, like an elephant's bath. ॥46॥
An elephant, once bathed, throws dust over itself again.
1428.18: The head shakes, the feet stumble, the eyes have lost their light; says Nanak, such is the state (he has come to), and still (man) is not absorbed in the Lord's sweetness. ॥47॥
1429.1: I regarded the world as my own, (yet here) no one is anyone's own. O Nanak, the Lord's devotion (alone) is lasting; keep it in your mind. ॥48॥
1429.2: All the world's creation is false: know this well, my friend. Says Nanak, it does not stand firm, like a wall of sand. ॥49॥
1429.3: Ram has gone, and Ravan has gone, who had a vast family. Says Nanak, nothing is lasting; the world is like a dream. ॥50॥
Ram and Ravan: in the Ramayana, Ram, the prince of Ayodhya, held to be an incarnation of Vishnu, and Ravan, the demon king of Lanka, whom Ram slew.
1429.4: Worry is for what is not meant to happen. This is the way of the world; O Nanak, no one stays for ever. ॥51॥
1429.5: Whatever has come into being will perish; all must pass, today or tomorrow. O Nanak, sing the Lord's praises, leaving all entanglements. ॥52॥
1429.6: Strength has gone, bonds have fallen (on me), and no means avails at all. Says Nanak, now the Lord is (my) shelter; (O Lord,) be (my) help, as (you were) for Gaj. ॥53॥
Gaj: in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant (Gajendra) seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free.
1429.7: Strength has come, the bonds are loosed, and every means avails. Says Nanak, (O Lord,) everything is in your hands; you alone are the help. ॥54॥
1429.8: Companions and friends have all gone and left (me); no one has stood by (me) to the end. Says Nanak, in this hour of trouble the one support is Raghunath (the Lord). ॥55॥
1429.9: The Naam remains, the Saadh (the holy one) remains, the Guru, Gobind, remains; says Nanak, in this world only a rare one has repeated the Guru's mantra. ॥56॥
1429.10: (I) have held fast in (my) heart the Name of Ram, which none can equal; remembering it, distress is erased, and the sight of you is granted. ॥57॥
